🌎 Plus: MapQuest soars again | Tuesday, September 01, 2026

PRESENTED BY OPENAI
 
Axios PM
By Mike Allen · Sep 01, 2026

Happy Tuesday! Today's newsletter, edited by Herb Scribner, is 605 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

🚨 Breaking: The House passed a short-term government funding bill through Dec. 11, avoiding a pre-election shutdown fight. Go deeper.

🛢️ Situational awareness: The U.S. military is conducting fresh strikes on Iranian targets in the area of the Strait of Hormuz, U.S. Central Command said.

  • A U.S. official said the idea is to reduce the risk of Iranian attacks on oil tankers, U.S. Navy ships and Air Force aircraft — to "mow the lawn," as the official put it. More from Barak Ravid.
 
 
1 big thing: Supercar crackdown
 
A yellow Lamborghini in London's West End last year. Photo: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images

You're not the only one getting ticked off by the loud Ferrari zooming through the neighborhood late at night or the giant Lamborghini blocking your parking spot on a busy street.

  • Why it matters: Supercars are fun and nice to look at. But when drivers rev their engines, clog up city streets and ignore their fines, it can create a real headache — both here in the U.S. and, recently, across the pond, The Wall Street Journal reports.

🇬🇧 Londoners are watching as many of these foreign supercars park outside Harrods, clog tight roads and pull over wherever they see fit, The Journal found.

  • The exotic rides are hogging taxi-only lanes and racing through some of the city's biggest neighborhoods.

⚠️ And it's driving residents mad. Some snap photos of the cars in illegal spots, and the drivers bite back.

  • "They more or less taunt us," London cabbie Mark Hart tells the WSJ.

🚦Earlier this month, London's Metropolitan Police said it had seized 90+ cars through the department's years-long crackdown against "antisocial driving behavior."

  • One of the cars, a Ferrari Monza SP2, was valued at nearly $5 million.

🏎️ In the U.S., supercars are fueling quality-of-life battles over their roaring engines, high speeds and racing capabilities.

  • Last month, Boston city officials voted to explore noise cameras after several complaints about loud cars and street racing.

2. 📈 Data center construction boom
 
Data: Census Bureau, FactSet. Chart: Matt Phillips/Axios

🚧 Construction spending on AI data center "shells" soared in July, rising at an annualized rate of nearly 60% from July 2025 levels, Axios' Matt Phillips writes.

  • Why it matters: It shows the AI-building frenzy was gathering strength this summer.

📊 By the numbers: Data center construction spending jumped to an annual pace of more than $75 billion in July, according to Census Bureau data out today.

  • That figure represents the value of the construction "put in place" during the month.

A family-owned tamales shop is expanding with ChatGPT
 
 

Inside a family run tamale business, three generations of the Ortega family use ChatGPT as the work grows more complex. From building a website to communicating with customers and employees, OpenAI helps them balance growth and tradition.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Texas highway sign on Interstate 610 in Houston today. Photo: Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images
  1. 🌀 The National Hurricane Center warns that Tropical Storm Edouard could become a hurricane by tomorrow as it is expected to make landfall in Texas and Louisiana. Get the latest.
  2. 🚓 A Bank of America vice president was killed yesterday in a deadly stabbing in Times Square that left one person injured and the suspect dead, Bloomberg reports.
  3. 📬 A whistleblower is alleging that the U.S. Postal Service defied court orders while rushing to build a new ballot system that could reject thousands of mail ballots, Axios' Andrew Pantazi and Donica Phifer report.
  4. 🏛️ Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial in Massachusetts told the judge they couldn't reach a verdict after 18 hours, but the judge instructed them to keep deliberating. Get the latest.
  5. 🍿 Netflix has a documentary coming about Trump's catering-truck escape from Air Force One, "Instadocs: The Decoy Plane," premiering Friday. Watch the trailer.
 
 
4. 📍1 for the road: MapQuest takeover
 
Photo: Mert Alper Dervis/Anadolu via Getty Images

📱 MapQuest (remember them?) skyrocketed to the top of Apple's app store after defying President Trump's call to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America."

  • The app surpassed Google Maps and Apple Maps in the app store, TechCrunch reports.

Read MapQuest's release.
